video_title: Joe Mazzulla on Cooper Flagg: "Pick Your Poison" | Celtics vs Maverick Pregame

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the defensive challenges of guarding Cooper Flagg
quotes.excerpt: he's a guy that you have to pick your poison, what you want to live with
quotes.quote: He's a guy that you have to pick your poison, what you want to live with, what you're willing to take away, and it just puts a ton of pressure on all three levels, especially the free throw line. When you get a young player that has the ability to draw fouls and put stress on your individual defense, it's a difference maker, and that's one of the biggest keys when you're playing against him is keeping him off the free throw line.
quotes.social_post: Joe Mazzulla on defending Cooper Flagg: You have to pick your poison. He puts a ton of pressure on all three levels and is a difference maker because of his ability to draw fouls and get to the free throw line.

structured.context: Joe Mazzulla discusses the defensive challenges of guarding Cooper Flagg during a pregame media availability.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on Jordan Walsh's offensive development this season
quotes.excerpt: Offensive rebounding, crash rate is up. It's also a little things
quotes.quote: Offensive rebounding, crash rate is up. It's also a little things like he does a great job of creating two-on-ones for other people when we get out in transition. That's some finishes at the rim. I think it's just continuing his screening and creating two-on-ones for us. It's important for us to, especially when they cross-match and they put different guys on him, he has to have the ability to be able to create two-on-ones for us. So, something he's gotten better at.
quotes.social_post: Joe Mazzulla says Jordan Walsh is improving his offensive game by focusing on crashing the boards and creating two on one situations for his teammates in transition.

structured.context: Joe Mazzulla evaluates the offensive development and transition play of Jordan Walsh.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on Jordan Walsh's defensive impact and role
quotes.excerpt: We're at our best when his defense at the point of attack is aggressive
quotes.quote: I don't think it has anything to do with starting. I think it's just the role we need him to have, regardless of whether he plays five minutes or 25 minutes. We're at our best when his defense at the point of attack is aggressive and he takes matchups personal and is willing to be the focal point of our defensive identity. So, it's a role that he's bought into, and when he's at his best, it takes our defense to a different level.
quotes.social_post: Joe Mazzulla on Jordan Walsh: We are at our best when his defense at the point of attack is aggressive and he takes matchups personal. It is a role he has bought into.

structured.context: Joe Mazzulla explains the importance of Jordan Walsh's defensive role regardless of his starting status or minutes played.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the team's defensive identity 12 games in
quotes.excerpt: Good, have to get better. Connected to one another, aggressive at the point of attack
quotes.quote: Good, have to get better. Connected to one another, aggressive at the point of attack and the screen, trying to force turnovers, getting a little bit better at defensive rebound, but got to get better, obviously.
quotes.social_post: Joe Mazzulla on the Celtics defensive identity 12 games into the season: We are connected and aggressive at the point of attack, but we still have to get better.

structured.context: Joe Mazzulla assesses the current state of the Celtics defensive identity 12 games into the season.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on defensive strategy regarding three-point attempts
quotes.excerpt: I don't really know what the numbers per se are. I think it's a matter of
quotes.quote: I don't really know what the numbers per se are. I think it's a matter of who we're giving them up to and where on the floor we're giving them up to, is the things that we look at the most. Every team has different schemes and personnel of different players. So, I think we try to be the best at making them take the ones that we want to and making the people that we want taking them, and making sure we get great contest.
quotes.social_post: Joe Mazzulla on defensive three point strategy: We try to be the best at making opponents take the shots we want them to take and ensuring we get great contests.

structured.context: Joe Mazzulla explains the team's defensive philosophy regarding three-point attempts and opponent shot selection.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on coaching Mitch and his basketball intelligence
quotes.excerpt: Very smart, in real time can pick up change, changing schemes throughout the game
quotes.quote: Very smart, in real time can pick up change, changing schemes throughout the game. He can pick up the cross-matches, can pick up the schemes, can pick up the different communications and the tendencies there. Offensively, still growing in the screening and some of the sets that we kind of do throughout the game, but to me, it's just his ability to recognize the information in real time and execute that, and something he takes pride in, and he's got to keep getting better.
quotes.social_post: Joe Mazzulla praises the basketball intelligence of Mitch: He can pick up changing schemes in real time and execute, which is something he takes pride in.

structured.context: Joe Mazzulla discusses the basketball intelligence and real-time decision-making of Mitch, referring to Neemias Queta.
